# A component with state of its own under a `for`, built at run time, whose
# var is named like a local of a component spliced into it: async.query's
# `match var got = r` beside the call site's `:value=got`. Spliced as it
# stood, the two `got`s were one name wherever a target spells a local bare,
# so html, fyne and gtk4 wrote `got = got` -- the answer never reached the
# var, or Go refused the program. A local of the spliced body whose name the
# call site reads is renamed, as its parameters already were
# (freshenShadowingParams).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
// async_query_loop.sngl, its card's var named `got`.

import async "sngl:async"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func lookup(name string) async.Result[int] {
    return {ok=name.length()}
}

// Each copy is an instance of its own: the instance is the key, so nothing
// caches per argument.
component card(name string) ui.node {
    var got option[int] = null
    async.query(on=name, fetch=lookup, :value=got)
    ui.text #len(value=got != null ? "{name} {got}" : name)
}

component cards ui.node {
    var names = ["blueberry", "fig"]
    var shown = true

    if shown {
        for var n = names {
            card #c(name=n)
        }
    }
    ui.button #add(text="Add", @click { names.push("grape") })
    ui.button #toggle(text="Toggle", @click { shown = !shown })
}

func testEachCopyAsksForItsOwn(t test.Test, c cards) {
    t.assert(c.c[0].len.value == "blueberry 9")
    t.assert(c.c[1].len.value == "fig 3")
    c.add.click()
    t.assert(c.c[2].len.value == "grape 5")
    t.assert(c.c[2].got == 5)
}

ui.window {
    cards()
}
